public_rationale: The March 27, 2023 technical report discloses broad principles but withholds detailed architecture and dataset-construction information [e2]. The March 30 CAIDP filing also reports these disclosure gaps [e1]. This supports the claim of substantial public opacity during the March–June 8, 2023 observation window [e1, e2]. It does not imply that researchers knew nothing: the report identifies GPT-4 as a Transformer trained to predict the next token [e2].
limitations: The evidence does not establish every confidential research-access arrangement.
No defined transparency scale establishes the literal superlative.
The CAIDP filing is an advocacy document, not a regulatory finding [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scientists lack access to how GPT-4 works and its training data, making it about as far from transparent as possible.

statement.excerpt: Bing relies on GPT-4, and we (eg, in the scientific community) don’t have access to how GPT-4 works, and we don’t have access to what data its trained on (vital, since we know that systems can bias eg political thought and hiring decisions based on those undisclosed data) — that’s about as far away from transparency as we could be.
statement.document_title: Two models of AI oversight - and how things could go deeply wrong

our_interpretation: The checkable core concerns public scientific access to GPT-4's detailed architecture, training process, and training dataset.
Knowing the general model family or being able to submit prompts does not constitute access to those details.
The transparency superlative is read as rhetorical emphasis on substantial opacity, not a measurable ranking of every possible disclosure policy.
The parenthetical discussion of political and hiring bias explains why transparency matters; it is not treated as a separate claim that GPT-4 caused a particular discriminatory decision.

There is no regular disclosure reporting period. I use the current GPT-4 release and documentation cycle, beginning in March 2023 and ending at the post. March 1 denotes the beginning of that month, not an asserted release day.
criteria.support_condition: The contemporaneous disclosure record withholds detailed architecture and training-dataset information from the general scientific community, despite allowing use or high-level study of the model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous records establish that the scientific community could inspect detailed architecture and the training dataset, rather than only model outputs or broad descriptions.

evidence.explanation: Section 2 explicitly withholds detailed architecture, model size, compute, dataset construction, and training-method information. The quoted abstract and Section 2 also disclose broad principles, data-source categories, and reinforcement learning from human feedback, qualifying any literal suggestion that nothing was known.
